paper.title: Language Generation: Complexity Barriers and Implications for Learning
paper.summary: Quantifies uniform sample thresholds for context-free, regular, locally threshold testable and non-erasing pattern languages.

formalization_scope.summary: All four numbered main theorems are addressed. Both parts of 4.1 and 5.1 are proved. Theorem 6.1 has the stated witnesses for positive n and a proved impossibility at zero.
specializations: Binary alphabets use Bool and an alphabet of size n uses Fin n.
Finite grammar production tables use numeric names. A promised algorithm is partial recursive.
Theorem 6.1 records exactly the positive-size range. The PaperMap documents this convention and the description-size conventions.

audit_refs.scope: Generated declaration and axiom checks for the four main theorems.

claims.title: No effective threshold for infinite context-free grammars
claims.statement_summary: Every partial recursive number-valued procedure fails to return a valid threshold on some pair of infinite context-free grammars.

formalization.notes: The input is a pair of finite CFG descriptions and termination is required only on the infinite-grammar promise.

claims.title: Double-exponential sample complexity for regular languages
claims.statement_summary: Proves the upper threshold for NFAs and regular expressions and a binary lower-bound family with both the stated DFA and regex presentation sizes.

formalization.notes: The same lower-bound family meets both description-size requirements for a single absolute constant.

lean_links.notes: The same lower-bound family meets both description-size requirements for a single absolute constant.

claims.title: Single-exponential sample complexity for locally threshold testable languages
claims.statement_summary: Proves the profile-size upper threshold and the two-profile obstruction for every alphabet size n ≥ 4.

formalization.notes: Both lower-bound languages are infinite and distinct. Their finite intersection contains all n! permutations.

lean_links.notes: Both lower-bound languages are infinite and distinct. Their finite intersection contains all n! permutations.

claims.title: Exponential obstruction for non-erasing pattern languages
claims.statement_summary: For every positive n, two infinite binary non-erasing pattern languages with pattern lengths 44n and 2 fail at threshold 2^n. The existence statement fails at n = 0.

source_assessment.notes: The printed quantifier ranges over natural numbers. Lean proves the exact positive-size range and rules out zero, where a length-zero pattern has finite language.
